## Goal
`draft_from_profile` (`src/freemyid/wizard/draft.py:606-631`, front end, in-house) fills the edit screens and `build_profile` (504-549) saves them, but no test calls `draft_from_profile`. It reads `allow_phone_disclosure` but not `allow_email_disclosure` or `removal_scope` (`src/freemyid/models.py:304-315`), so an edit may silently drop them.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. For fake profiles covering a middle name and suffix, nicknames, two previous names, three addresses with one current, DOB versus age only, phones/emails/relatives, every permission flag, each `email_mode`, schedule values and each consent basis: `build_profile(draft_from_profile(p))` equals `p` on every user-entered field (compare `model_dump` minus ids and timestamps, with any exclusion listed and explained in the test).
2. Each field lost in the round trip (for example `allow_email_disclosure`, `removal_scope`, previous-name suffixes) is its own strict xfail citing the `draft.py` line as a finding.
3. `keep_consent=False` leaves `existing_consent` unset; `keep_consent=True` keeps the original consent, text version included (627-628).
4. The draft never holds a mailbox secret: `draft.mailbox` has no password or `keyring_service` (623-626) and `saved_password` is a bool (`_has_saved_password` monkeypatched; never touch a real keyring).

Fake data only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Offline: no network, no sockets (FastAPI `TestClient` is fine), no git, no installs, no new dependencies. Tests must pass on Windows CI too: `tmp_path` and `pathlib`, no hard-coded `/tmp`, no `/`-joined path strings or other POSIX-only assumptions (WO-217 broke windows-latest that way). The module under test is outside Codex's code lane: a real product bug = `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)` plus a finding with file:line in VENDOR_STATUS.md; never edit it. Check `tests/`, `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/` and `tests/grok/` first and don't duplicate a guard. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing; re-check them in your worktree.
